title: Holdback Strategy and Observation Log (personal scratchpad)
content:
Context: quick personal notes for an upcoming release where we keep a 5% holdback cohort for the new model binary + opt kernel. This is a working scratchpad — not polished.

Goals:
- Validate user-visible latency and token-cost impact for 24h at low volume.
- Catch regressions in tokenization edge cases (recent segfault fix).
- Keep roll-forward path simple if metrics look good; rollback if p95 latency > baseline + 120ms for >30m.

Planned rollout sequence (fast reference):
1) Push model v2.3.1 to staging pool (smoke tests).
2) Canary internal traffic: 1% traffic to pool-v2.3.1 for 2h. Watch success rate.
3) Holdback: create holdback cohort = 5% of users (cookie-based steering) -> route to pool-v2.3.1 for 24h.
4) If stable, increase to 20% for 6h. Then 50% for 2h. Then full.

Holdback specifics:
- Cohort assignment: cookie "rwd_holdback_v2" -> seeded hash modulo 100 < 5. Implementation note: edge router supports "percent_split" with explicit seed. Use seed=230925 for reproducibility.
- Pinning: persist model_version key in rollout metadata so retries are deterministic. Command to pin from control-plane: curl -X POST $API/rollout/pin -d '{ "model": "serving-model-v2.3.1", "routes": ["chat"] }' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Eviction TTL for evicted kernels: 10m (to allow short bursts without cold start thrash).

Metrics to watch (dashboard quick list):
- request_success_rate (per-route, per-model) — alert if <99.5% sustained for 15m
- latency_p95 and latency_p99 token-time (per-model) — alert if p95 > baseline + 120ms for 30m
- tokens_per_request and tokens_per_minute (cost signal) — watch for spike due to degenerate prompts
- OOM / eviction counters on nodes running pool-v2.3.1
- Model-output divergence metric (eval harness): mismatch_rate vs baseline -> handy quick-run: /tools/evals/run_eval --suite=p0_prompts --model=serving-model-v2.3.1

Quick queries / commands (notes-to-self):
- P95 over last 30m for route "chat":
  SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) FROM requests WHERE route='chat' AND model='serving-model-v2.3.1' AND ts > now() - interval '30 minutes';
- Find user buckets assigned to holdback:
  SELECT count(*) FROM routing_assignments WHERE cohort='holdback_v2_seed230925' AND assigned_at > now() - interval '1 day';
- Force-unpin (if emergency): curl -X POST $API/rollout/unpin -d '{"routes":["chat"]}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Rollback criteria (hard):
- request_success_rate <98% for >10m OR
- p99 latency > baseline + 400ms for >15m OR
- any memory OOMs exceeding 3 across pool nodes in 30m
If rollback triggered:
- Immediately scale down pool-v2.3.1 to 0% traffic (control-plane API).
- Pin previous stable: serving-model-v2.2.8 as emergency fallback.
- Postmortem start: notify #eng-incident and create ticket with logs and trace ids.

Open questions / TODOs (unresolved):
- How to expose holdback cohort membership in trace logs without leaking PII? Need to confirm hashing-only id ok with privacy team. (ask @Liam)
- Should we add an automated snapshot of kv-cache-hit-rate per model for 24h? Might be instructive for token cost analysis.
- Confirm the TTL for kernel eviction is compatible with dedicated capacity policies (ops: @Ethan).

Observations during previous tiny rollout (notes):
- Observed a 30ms median regression when quantized kernel used on A100s vs ampere-optimized kernel on same HW — small but consistent.
- Two requests triggered tokenizer fallback from new token mapping; fixed by rolling patched token table but still worth watching.

Post-release checklist (if holdback OK -> widen):
- Capture final eval run and attach to JIRA ticket.
- Run cost simulation for projected prod qps for 30/60/90 days.
- Update runbook with exact curl commands and emergency contacts.
- Document cohort seed and store in rollout metadata.

Notes to self: keep this doc ephemeral. After release, extract a cleaned sequence into the team rollout guide (confluence). If rollback happens, save this scratchpad snapshot into the incident ticket.

-- nina
